# Nativele

> Designed for AI agents. Driven by TypeScript. Defined in vanilla HTML. A lightweight library for building web components: bind HTML templates to TypeScript custom elements. HTML describes structure and where data goes; TypeScript owns state and behavior; the DOM is the only view. Fully typed by tsc, no virtual DOM, no bundler required.

Workflow: write `x.html` + `x.ts`, then run `npx ts-dom check`. It regenerates `x.html.ts`, runs tsc (or vue-tsc when the project has it) and lint, and points errors at the template; `--a11y` adds the accessibility checks.

Every diagnostic is `file:line:col severity [rule-id] message` and ends with a `Fix:` hint: read the hint and apply it. Each rule below is one line; its guide section has the details.

## Template syntax (HTML only names things; no expressions)
- `{{ name }}`: text hole, a single identifier (NOT `{{ a.b }}` / `{{ a + 1 }}`), never in an attribute: [templates](docs/templates.md#html-syntax).
- `data-ref="x"`: the element as `this.refs.x`, typed by its tag; on a `<form>`, `elements.<name>` is typed too (`RadioNodeList` for a shared name, a misspelled name is a tsc error): [templates](docs/templates.md#html-syntax), [reading a form](docs/components.md#reading-a-form).
- `data-if="x"`: hidden by default (removed from the DOM, kept in memory); shown when `x` is truthy or by `this.show("x", true)`: [templates](docs/templates.md#html-syntax).
- `<template data-each="x">`: a list with exactly one root element; never nested, no `<slot>` in it, no `data-if` on its root, not inside `<svg>` or `<math>` (`each-in-svg`); an item's `el` is typed by its root tag: [lists](docs/lists.md#items-as-plain-elements-replace).
- Per-row state of the parent (selected, rank) is a separate prop of the item component, set on each row through `this.lists.x.get(key)` (`row.el.selected = ...`), so only changed rows render: [lists](docs/lists.md#per-row-state-selected-rank).
- `data-on-<event>="method"`: a lowercase event name and a method name only; calls the public `method(e, hit: EventHit)`, checked against the template: [events](docs/components.md#events-data-on-).
- A handler's `e` is typed as the event it receives: `EmitEvent<Child, "name">` on a child component tag, else the DOM type (`click` is a `PointerEvent`): [events](docs/components.md#events-data-on-).
- Never name a handler like a DOM or Nativele member (`remove`, `click`, `set`, `render`): [events](docs/components.md#events-data-on-).
- `<slot name="x">`: Light DOM by default, where the slots take only content written in HTML (the children at build, and what a parent template's list or `data-if` puts in); native with `shadow: true`: [Slots in Light mode](docs/components.md#slots-in-light-mode).
- `data-on-*` handles events that reach the component root; an element moved out of it (a `<dialog>` in `document.body`) no longer triggers them: [events](docs/components.md#events-data-on-).
- `<style>` only at the top level of the file; `<style scoped>` limits it to the component in Light DOM: [styles](docs/components.md#styles).
- Another component: write its tag; the generated module imports it: [composition](docs/components.md#composition-using-multiple-components-together).

## Component (TypeScript)
```ts
import { Component, define, event } from "@nativele/ts-dom";
import type { EmitEvent, EventHit } from "@nativele/ts-dom";
import tpl from "./counter.html.js";

class MyCounter extends Component(tpl, {
  state: { count: 0 },                         // owned by the component, changed only with this.set()
  props: { step: 1 },                          // owned by the parent, read-only here
  derive: { double: (s) => s.count * 2 },      // usable by {{ double }} / data-if
  emits: { "count-change": event<{ count: number }>() },   // events sent up
  // shadow: true,                             // optional Shadow DOM
}) {
  inc() {                                      // referenced by data-on-click="inc"
    this.set((s) => ({ count: s.count + this.props.step }));
    this.emit("count-change", { count: this.state.count });
  }
  override render(view, changed) { /* lists, attributes, focus */ }
}
define("my-counter", MyCounter);
```
The compiler rejects these, and each error names the template (`template: "card.html"`): [safeguards](docs/components.md#safeguards-in-types-and-at-runtime).
- A hole or `data-if` name missing from state, props and derive (`missingStateKeys`).
- A name used twice (`conflictingKeys`).
- A prop named like an element member (`reservedPropNames`).
- An emitted native event name (`nativeEventNames`).
- A missing `data-on-*` method (`missingHandlers`), or a handler parameter the bound event cannot satisfy (`wrongHandlerParameters`).
- `any`, also inferred (as from `JSON.parse`), in state, props, derive, an emitted detail, a handler or its event parameter, or the template (`anyInContract`; `ts-dom check` rule `any-in-contract`): declare the type, or `unknown` and narrow it, and import the template from its `./x.html.js` module.

## Data flow (one direction)
- `state`, `props`, `render`'s `view` and `derive`'s argument are `DeepReadonly`: replace objects (`{ ...item, done: true }`), never change them in place: [state](docs/components.md#data-and-view-state-optional).
- Change state only with `this.set(patch | s => patch)`: it merges shallowly, renders synchronously, and does nothing when no field changed; `this.batch(fn)` combines updates: [state](docs/components.md#data-and-view-state-optional).
- A `derive` function gets state and props merged and cannot read another derived value: [state](docs/components.md#data-and-view-state-optional).
- Lists, attributes and focus go in `render(view, changed)`; guard each part with `changed.has("x")` and annotate `changed` with the names you check (`ReadonlySet<"items" | "visible">`), never `ReadonlySet<string>`: [state](docs/components.md#data-and-view-state-optional).
- With `state`, `props` or `derive`, every `{{ hole }}` and `data-if` outside a list item names one of them; show store data by copying it into state in the `bind` callback: [recipes](docs/recipes.md#showing-data-from-a-store).
- Props go down: the parent sets them by attribute or typed property (`this.refs.child.value = v.x`); a component never assigns its own props: [data flow](docs/components.md#data-flow-props-down-events-up).
- Events go up: `emit` does not bubble; the parent handles it with `data-on-<event>` on the child tag with a handler typed `onX(e: EmitEvent<Child, "name">)` (no cast): [data flow](docs/components.md#data-flow-props-down-events-up).
- A wrapper element catches only an event declared `event<...>({ bubbles: true })`.
- A misspelled `data-on-*` on a native element (`<form data-on-submt>`) is `unknown-native-event`: [misspelled event names](docs/tooling.md#misspelled-event-names).
- Data needed several levels away goes in a shared `createStore` that components `bind`; never forward props or re-emit events (`prop-forwarding`, `emit-forwarding`): [shared stores](docs/components.md#avoiding-layer-by-layer-passing-lint-ts-domdata-flow).
- `store.set` replaces the whole value (`this.set` merges): `store.set((s) => ({ ...s, status: "loading" }))`: [stores](docs/components.md#state-store-when-not-using-state).
- Call `bind`, `on` and `onCleanup` in `connected()`, never in the constructor: [stores](docs/components.md#state-store-when-not-using-state).
- Set the element's own class and attributes in `connected()`; a constructor that does it makes a browser create an unknown element (`constructor-host-change`): [components](docs/components.md#components).
- Export the class passed to `define()`, or its tag is left out of `ts-dom-tags.ts` (`define-class-not-exported`): [checks](docs/tooling.md#errors-at-the-template).
- Cancel a component's own request on removal: an `AbortController` made in `connected()`, aborted from `onCleanup`, `AbortError` ignored: [recipes](docs/recipes.md#cancelling-a-request-when-the-component-is-removed).
- Write a form control's value in `render` only when it differs (`unguarded-input-value`): [form inputs](docs/components.md#a-small-reminder-about-form-inputs).
- Write fixed structure in the template, not with `document.createElement` (`static-markup-in-code`), and keep data in state, not DOM nodes (`dom-node-in-state`): [design](docs/design.md#design-principles).
- Loading and error states, modal dialogs, form validation, filtered lists: [recipes](docs/recipes.md) and `examples/recipes/` in the repository.
- A table whose columns come from a config array: [recipes](docs/recipes.md#a-table-with-configurable-columns).
- A component that is a control of a native `<form>`: [recipes](docs/recipes.md#a-form-control-of-your-own).
- Re-rendering text when the locale changes: [recipes](docs/recipes.md#switching-the-language).
- Components of another package in a template: lint checks them when the template's package depends on that package and it lists `@nativele/ts-dom`; `ts-dom gen` writes imports only from the scanned folders: [Nativele component packages](docs/tooling.md#nativele-component-packages).
- A custom element from another library in a template: [components](docs/components.md#custom-elements-from-other-libraries). When its package declares a custom elements manifest (`customElements` in its package.json), lint checks attribute, event and slot names against it: [custom elements manifests](docs/tooling.md#custom-elements-manifests).
- `unchecked-custom-elements` and `unchecked-content` name the custom elements lint cannot read, each cause with its fix; once the elements are right, silence them with `--ignore=<id>`: [custom elements lint cannot read](docs/tooling.md#custom-elements-lint-cannot-read).

## Template without a component
`tpl.instantiate()` returns `{ root, rootElement, refs, lists, text, show }` for pieces created in code; `data-on-*` is inert and `<slot>` is not projected there: [templates](docs/templates.md#templates-without-a-component).

## Lists
- An item with anything of its own (state, events, a nested list) is a component filled with `items =`; an item of a few texts and `data-if` is plain elements filled with `replace()`: [lists](docs/lists.md#lists).
- Items as components: `<template data-each="todos" data-key="id" data-prop="todo"><todo-row role="listitem"></todo-row></template>`, `this.lists.todos.items = view.todos` in `render`, `hit: EventHit<Todo, "id">` in handlers; the item component is exported and declares `todo` in `props`: [items as components](docs/lists.md#items-as-components-items--).
- Assign new item objects: an item that is the same object as last time does not update its component: [items as components](docs/lists.md#items-as-components-items--).
- Items as plain elements: no `data-key` or `data-prop`; `this.lists.x.replace(items, keyFn, (item, { text, refs, show, el }) => ...)`: [plain items](docs/lists.md#items-as-plain-elements-replace).
- Without `moveBefore` a moved item is disconnected and connected again: [moving items](docs/lists.md#moving-items-connecting-and-subscriptions).
- Full example (add, remove, sort, toggle, child emit): `examples/readme/task-board.ts` and `task-row.ts` in the repository.

## Rules for agents
- Before working on Nativele components, run `npx ts-dom skills nativele-core` and follow it.
- `npx ts-dom skills` lists the Skills shipped with the package and shows which ones cover the project's dependencies; `npx ts-dom skills <name>` prints one: [Skills](README.md#nativele-skills).
- `npx ts-dom rules --explain=<id>` (or `rules --json`) explains any rule id from a diagnostic: why it exists, a wrong example and the fix.
- Markup well-formedness is a formatter's job (`oxfmt --check`): [checks](docs/tooling.md#checks). With a formatter, generate with `--whitespace=collapse`: [whitespace](docs/tooling.md#whitespace).
- If checks behave oddly (no types, a template not found), run `npx ts-dom doctor --json` first; fix each issue by its `Fix:` hint: [doctor](docs/tooling.md#ts-dom-doctor).
- `npx ts-dom gen --check` (writes nothing, exit 1) tells whether the generated files are stale before you trust `tsc` errors.
- After any `.html` or component change run `npx ts-dom check --json` and fix every issue by its `Fix:` hint; never cast a type error away.

## Setup
```sh
npm i -D typescript && npm i @nativele/ts-dom
npx ts-dom gen && npx tsc          # tsconfig: module/moduleResolution NodeNext (or bundler), lib includes DOM, strict true (doctor warns when it is false, or left out on TypeScript 5)
```
In a browser without a bundler map the bare name once: `<script type="importmap">{"imports":{"@nativele/ts-dom":"/node_modules/@nativele/ts-dom/dist/index.mjs"}}</script>`; relative imports in your own code need `.js` extensions. With Vite, `@nativele/ts-dom/vite` is optional: [setup](docs/tooling.md#installation-and-setup).

## Pitfalls
- Import templates with `./x.html.js`, not `./x.html`, and run `ts-dom gen` before `tsc`: [setup](docs/tooling.md#installation-and-setup).
- Never edit `x.html.ts` or `ts-dom-tags.ts`; most projects git-ignore them: [generated files](docs/tooling.md#generated-files).
- `export class` a component to get typed `refs.child` in parent templates: [composition](docs/components.md#composition-using-multiple-components-together).
- `package.json` needs `"type": "module"` (with `tsc` emitting NodeNext, and with Vite): [setup](docs/tooling.md#installation-and-setup).
- `slotchange()` is Light DOM only; with `shadow: true` use the native `slotchange` event: [Light and Shadow](docs/components.md#light-default-and-shadow).
- A Light DOM component builds its content when connected (a `shadow: true` one in the constructor), so a new element has no children, `refs` or `text` until it is appended: [components](docs/components.md#components).
- Children a framework renders go into a `shadow: true` component; a Light DOM component leaves what is added after it is built outside its slots (`unplaced-child`): [framework children](docs/components.md#slots-and-children-managed-by-a-framework).
